body:
### Problem

When returning to OpenHands after some time away, all conversations are idle and must be woken up one at a time: each conversation has to be opened/clicked individually just to resume its agent. With many conversations open this is tedious busywork before any real work can start.

Waking them up front isn't great either — agent startup is currently slow enough that eagerly resuming everything is unattractive. (Making startup much faster would be the other fix, but that's a bigger lift.)

### Proposed solution

Add a **"Wake all agents"** button to the conversation list / workspace UI that resumes every idle conversation in one action, so a returning user doesn't have to click through each conversation just to bring their agents back.

Nice-to-haves (optional):
- Progress feedback while the batch wake runs (e.g. "3/7 resumed")
- A per-conversation wake affordance visible in the list, so a user can wake a subset without opening each conversation
- Configurable behavior on startup (e.g. auto-wake all vs. manual button) for users who want it

### Alternatives considered

- Clicking into each conversation to wake it — what exists today; doesn't scale past a handful of conversations
- Speeding up startup so eager wake is cheap — worth doing too, but the button helps regardless
- A background auto-wake on app load — may surprise users with resource usage; a button keeps it explicit

### Related issues

- #16752 — idle conversations look the same as actively working ones (a wake affordance would pair well with clearer idle state)
- #18057 — live multi-agent activity view

---
_This issue was created by an AI agent (OpenHands) on behalf of the user._

<!-- openhands-ai-triage:start -->
---
## OpenHands AI triage
**The following comments and acceptance criteria were added by the OpenHands AI agent.**

### Triage
Frontend feature for the Agent Canvas conversation list: a single control in the conversation panel that resumes every resumable paused conversation in one action, so a returning user does not have to open each conversation individually. Canvas owns this UI; no new Agent Server endpoint is required — the batch wake must reuse the existing per-conversation resume path (`resumeConversation` in `src/hooks/mutation/conversation-mutation-utils.ts`, which already covers the local runtime and the Cloud paused-sandbox resume). The candidate set is the conversations the list already shows as paused/stopped: those whose `execution_status` is `PAUSED` (set by the existing stop/pause flow on both backends), plus Cloud conversations whose `sandbox_status` is `PAUSED`. Conversations that the list treats as unresumable (runtime missing, counted as archived per `F04.show-archived-unarchive`) are excluded.

Non-goals: no change to Agent Server endpoints or wire contracts; no automatic wake on app load; no per-conversation wake affordance in the list rows; no progress UI beyond a single completion summary; no change to startup speed or the F04 thread-scope filter.

### Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The expanded conversation list shows a "Wake all agents" control whenever at least one resumable paused conversation is visible in the panel, and it is absent (or disabled) when there are none, so the button reflects real resumable state.
- [ ] Activating the control resumes every resumable paused conversation that is loaded into the conversation panel, including pinned ones, without opening any conversation; conversations in other execution states (running, idle, finished, errored) are not touched.
- [ ] Paused conversations not yet loaded into the panel (beyond the first 20 conversations) are also resumed by the same action; the feature must not silently skip conversations that are merely unloaded, and the scope covered by one activation is discoverable to the user.
- [ ] After the batch wake completes, every successfully resumed conversation shows in the list with the same state a single-conversation resume produces today (no longer paused), verified by the list refresh that follows resume.
- [ ] If a conversation fails to resume (for example, its runtime is missing or unreachable), that conversation is left in its prior state, the rest of the batch still resumes, and the user sees a failure indication naming the affected conversation(s) or count.
- [ ] The action is safe to run when nothing is resumable: activating with zero resumable paused conversations changes no conversation state and surfaces a "nothing to wake" outcome rather than an unhandled error.
- [ ] The behavior works on both backend kinds — local agent-server conversations and Cloud conversations (Cloud via the existing paused-sandbox resume) — without Cloud-only or local-only special cases in the user-visible flow.
- [ ] New user-facing strings are added to `src/i18n/translation.json` for all locales via the standard i18n workflow (`npm run make-i18n`), and the button/menu text is localized rather than hardcoded.
- [ ] Behavior coverage is added at the service/mutation level following the repository TDD baseline (mock the underlying service, not the consuming hook), and `npm run lint`, `npm test`, and `npm run build` pass with the change.

<!-- triage-source:c44122a8d445a71c5013c8a1b2204b21b5461dd3853713d181b5d58fcfe06668 -->
<!-- openhands-ai-triage:end -->
title: [Feature]: "Wake all agents" button to resume all idle conversations at once

body:
### Problem

The first onboarding step, **“Choose your Agent,”** offers OpenHands, Claude Code, Codex, and Gemini CLI without explaining what is actually being selected.

This can easily be interpreted as choosing an LLM provider, model family, or subscription-based authentication method. In reality, the selection determines the **agent harness or agent implementation** that Agent Canvas runs. Model and authentication configuration are handled separately.

This distinction is important because selecting “Codex,” for example, means running the Codex harness through ACP—not running the OpenHands harness with an OpenAI model.

### Suggested improvement

Rename the step to something clearer, such as:

> Choose your agent harness

Add a short explanation:

> This selects the agent implementation that will execute tasks. Model and authentication settings are configured separately.

The options could also include short descriptions:

* **OpenHands:** OpenHands agent with a separately configured LLM
* **Claude Code:** Claude Code harness through ACP
* **Codex:** Codex harness through ACP
* **Gemini CLI:** Gemini CLI harness through ACP
title: [UX]: Clarify that “Choose your Agent” selects the agent harness

body:
### Problem or Use Case

Selecting an agent profile currently also selects conversation-backed execution. Those are separate concerns: a deterministic automation script may need only the profile's selected credentials, while an agent run needs the profile's model, tools, secrets, conversation, and runtime.

This coupling forces a scheduled scanner that only queries an external API to create an agent conversation and, in Docker mode, a container. The scanner should run as ordinary automation code. Only agent work selected by the scanner should acquire a conversation runtime.

### Desired Behavior

Store an explicit execution mode on automation definitions and snapshot it on queued runs, independently from the selected agent profile.

- Script mode executes the bundle without creating a conversation and passes the selected profile only to the Agent Server's profile-scoped command API.
- Agent mode retains profile-backed conversation execution for prompt and plugin presets.
- Existing profile-backed definitions keep their previous agent behavior after migration.
- Raw automation definitions default to script mode.

The Automation service continues to use software-agent-sdk for every Agent Server operation. No extension should inspect the local/Docker workspace kind.

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Profile selection and execution mode are independent fields in create, update, response, run history, and Git sync schemas.
- [ ] A profile-backed script runs without creating a conversation or Docker runtime.
- [ ] A profile-backed agent run creates a conversation using the existing conversation backend.
- [ ] Prompt and plugin presets select agent mode; raw definitions default to script mode.
- [ ] Existing profile-backed definitions migrate to agent mode without changing behavior.
- [ ] Webhook and scheduled runs snapshot both fields when queued.
- [ ] Script command dispatch uses the typed software-agent-sdk profile-scoped command parameter.
- [ ] Local tests cover backend selection, persistence, migration, and command dispatch.

### Additional Context

This depends on software-agent-sdk #5046 for profile-scoped script commands. It is a prerequisite for #463, where a script scanner submits selected work to separate agent runs.
title: Separate profile credential scope from agent execution

## Feedback from Operum User

**Type:** Feature Request

### Description

Let the user choose a custom working directory for each agent, instead of always using the default disk location.

### Motivation

1. **Disk space (primary reason).** The default disk where agent worktrees/working folders live can run low on space, especially with multiple agents/teams running repos of meaningful size. Being able to point an agent's working directory at a different disk/volume would relieve that.
2. **Parallel execution speed (secondary, less important).** Spreading agents' working folders across different disks could help I/O contention when several agents run in parallel, though this is a nice-to-have compared to the space concern.

### Requested behavior

- Per-agent setting (not just global) to choose the working directory location.
- When changing/setting the working directory, let the user choose between:
  - **Copy** the existing working folder/contents to the new location, or
  - **Re-create** fresh at the new location (new clone/checkout rather than copying existing state).

### Context

Raised directly by the founder of an active team, as a direct request to file this feedback.

---
*Filed on behalf of the user — PM agent*


---
*Filed by Operum's PM agent.*
title: Allow choosing a custom working directory per agent

body:
## Summary

**Reviewer and QA automations** need to show where each GitHub comment came from.

When an automation posts a review or QA report, maintainers should be able to see:

- LLM profile, profile details
- conversation trajectories; including prompts, skills
- (maybe) which automation run produced the comment

This was available with the old GitHub Actions flow because everyone could open the workflow run and inspect logs and artifacts. With Cloud Automation, this became a black box. With experiments, these change in random ways.

## Problem

Maintainers need clear information _what ran via automation_, in order to assess how reliable or complete it was; or, e.g. when an automated review is too harsh or odd or unexpectedly lenient.

<Summary> Recent example </summary>
<details>
- 2 automation runs appeared to run on the same PR
- one run used GPT-5.5 and another used Minimax
- both runs appeared to stop
- the GitHub comments did not clearly show the LLM profile or model
- the comments did not link to a public or shared trace, log or archive

This makes it harder to debug review quality, compare model variants, understand failures and explain automation behaviour.
</details>

## Solution

1. Display LLM Profile
2. Make available conversation trajectories: via download or via public share

## 1: Display LLM Profile 

Add a footer to top-level GitHub reviewer and QA comments.

Example:

```md
---
This review was performed by OpenHands Cloud Automation.
LLM profile: `gpt-5.5-reviewer`
Resolved model: `litellm_proxy/openai/gpt-5.5`
Automation run: `.../automations/{automation_id}/runs/{run_id}`
Conversation: `https://app.all-hands.dev/conversations/{conversation_id}`  # public share
Logs or archive: (download link)
<!-- openhands-automation-run:{run_id} -->
```

A/B tests should clearly mark the comment with the selected variant.

<summary> Implementation notes: </summary>
<details>
- keep `AUTOMATION_MODEL` if needed, but document that it means the selected profile
- consider adding `AUTOMATION_MODEL_PROFILE` as a clearer alias
- set the resolved model after the preset script calls `workspace.get_llm()`
- build conversation and run URLs after the conversation exists
- update the PR review and QA prompts or plugins to append the footer when values are present

</details>

## 2: Conversation Trajectories: Download Alternative

Add a durable artifact for each automation run, similar to GitHub Actions artifacts.

In `OpenHands/OpenHands`, there is an authenticated conversation export endpoint:

```http
GET /api/v1/app-conversations/{conversation_id}/download
```

<summary> New Automation Download Endpoint? </summary>
<details>
If we want a new download for automations specifically (why?), the artifact could include:
- a conversation trajectory export
- metadata JSON with automation ID, run ID, event ID, model profile, resolved model, timestamps, status and error details
- plugin and preset versions
- (maybe) Laminar trace IDs when available

Possible API:

- `GET /api/automation/v1/runs/{run_id}/artifacts`
- `GET /api/automation/v1/runs/{run_id}/artifacts/{artifact_id}`

Possible storage shape:

- `automation_run_artifacts` table
- fields for run ID, artifact kind, storage path, content type, size, created time, expiry time and visibility

</details>

## 3: Conversation Trajectories: Public Sharing Alternative

For public repositories, OpenHands-maintained reviewer and QA automations are needed in the open.

We could use `public conversation sharing` from the enterprise app server.

<summary> Additional notes for other automation users than OpenHands repos </summary>
<details>
Default visibility should be configurable by organization.

Suggested visibility options
- `private`: only authenticated OpenHands users with access can view
- `repo` or `org`: only authorized repository or organization users can view
- `public`: anyone with the link can view a sanitized trace or archive
</details>

<details>
<summary>Investigation notes</summary>

### What the automation service already has

- `Automation.model` stores the selected model profile in `openhands/automation/models.py`, `schemas.py` and `preset_router.py`.
- the dispatcher passes that profile into runs as `AUTOMATION_MODEL`.
- the dispatcher also includes the profile in `AUTOMATION_EVENT_PAYLOAD.model`.
- prompt and plugin preset scripts read `AUTOMATION_MODEL`.
- those scripts call `workspace.get_llm(profile_name=model_profile)`.
- those scripts print the selected profile and resolved `llm.model` to stdout.
- preset conversations use `delete_on_close=False`, so conversation history should survive completion.
- preset scripts inject `AUTOMATION_SESSION_URL` as a secret in cloud mode.
- `AUTOMATION_SESSION_URL` is not automatically added to GitHub review or QA comments.
- the automation frontend links an activity-log item to `/conversations/{conversation_id}` when `AutomationRun.conversation_id` exists.
- `AutomationRunResponse` exposes `conversation_id`, `sandbox_id` and `bash_command_id`.
- the run API does not expose a first-class artifact, log or archive URL.

### What the old GitHub Actions flow provided

In `OpenHands/extensions`:

- `plugins/pr-review/action.yml` selects and logs the model.
- it passes `LLM_MODEL` into the agent.
- it provides `REVIEW_RUN_URL`.
- it uploads log artifacts, including `*.log` and `output/`.
- it also uploads Laminar trace information.
- `plugins/pr-review/scripts/prompt.py` includes a feedback footer with the GitHub Actions workflow run URL.
- that footer does not include the selected model or profile.
- `plugins/qa-changes/action.yml` logs the model and uploads logs and trace artifacts.
- `plugins/qa-changes/scripts/prompt.py` tells the agent how to post a QA report.
- the QA prompt does not include the same provenance footer.

Cloud Automation needs an equivalent or better way to inspect each run.

### Existing archive or export capability nearby

In `OpenHands/OpenHands`, there is an authenticated conversation export endpoint:

```http
GET /api/v1/app-conversations/{conversation_id}/download
```

</details>

---

This issue was created and rewritten by an AI agent (OpenHands) on behalf of the user.
title: Reviewer agent and QA Agent: add LLM, trajectories

body:
### Problem or Use Case

Agent-backed automations currently have two incomplete execution paths. Event triggers can route later events to a deterministic subject conversation, but scheduled or programmatic automations cannot submit work for a subject through the same machinery. Extension workers therefore decode Agent Server URLs and session keys and attach to `RemoteConversation` themselves. This duplicates lifecycle code across extensions, exposes runtime details at the wrong layer, and makes local and Docker execution harder to keep identical.

GitHub issue, pull-request, and thread automations need a stable conversation per external subject. A poller should be able to identify a subject such as repository ID plus pull-request number and ask the Automation service to create or resume its conversation. The role implementation should only select work and provide the next turn.

### Desired Behavior

Add a service-owned subject-turn operation that reuses the existing `subject_key`, `conversation_id_for`, subject locking, coalescing, and `continue_conversation` behavior.

The scanner remains an ordinary automation script: it needs neither a conversation nor a Docker runtime. Profile selection scopes the saved credentials available to that script and is independent of execution mode. Only the child agent work created by this operation provisions a local or Docker conversation runtime.

The caller supplies a stable opaque subject key, source, turn text, and idempotency key. The Automation service namespaces the key by organization and automation, creates the first conversation with the automation's selected agent profile, or appends and wakes the existing conversation. The service serializes turns for one subject and reports whether a request created, delivered, queued, or deduplicated work.

Expose the operation through the Automation service API. Authentication must restrict a running automation to submitting turns for itself. Agent Server operations continue through software-agent-sdk; conversation creation, attachment, profile resolution, secrets, local/Docker selection, wake-up, and cleanup remain outside extension code.

Event triggers continue using the existing declarative `destination: continue_conversation` path. Scheduled pollers use the same subject-turn operation programmatically. A GitHub reviewer can use the immutable repository ID plus PR number as its subject key and the head SHA as its idempotency key.

Subject conversations must have a bounded lifecycle: concurrent events are coalesced, closed/released subjects no longer route to an old runtime, and idle Docker resources can be reclaimed without silently attaching to an unrelated conversation.

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A typed subject-turn request accepts `source`, `subject_key`, `turn`, `idempotency_key`, and `wake_agent` without accepting an arbitrary conversation ID.
- [ ] The first request creates a deterministic conversation with the automation's selected agent profile; another request for the same subject resumes it, while different subjects and different automations remain isolated.
- [ ] Duplicate idempotency keys do not deliver the same turn twice, and concurrent requests for one subject cannot create multiple conversations.
- [ ] A running automation receives credentials that can submit subject turns only for its own automation and cannot attach to arbitrary conversations.
- [ ] Extension code does not need Agent Server URLs, runtime session keys, workspace-kind checks, profile loading, or `RemoteConversation.attach`.
- [ ] A profile-backed scanner runs without creating a conversation; only submitted agent work acquires a conversation runtime.
- [ ] Event-triggered and programmatic subject turns share the existing routing and coalescing implementation.
- [ ] Local and Docker-backed tests exercise the same public contract, including wake-up, failure, release, and bounded cleanup behavior.
- [ ] Agent Server communication uses software-agent-sdk rather than private HTTP calls.

### Additional Context

This builds on the execution boundary in #464 and tracked agent-turn runs in #465, and completes the general capability introduced by #362 rather than adding a second conversation identity system. It is needed to simplify agent-backed extensions such as GitHub issue triage and PR review, which should contain GitHub policy but no runtime attachment code.
title: Add service-owned subject turns for agent-backed automations

body:
### Problem or Use Case

The Automation service can dispatch an automation bundle into a conversation runtime, and event triggers can append follow-up messages to an existing subject conversation. It cannot represent agent work selected by a deterministic scanner as a separate tracked run. Reusing the scanner's own run would couple orchestration code to the agent conversation and prevent one scanner from starting several independent jobs.

### Desired Behavior

Add an internal service-owned agent-turn run. It stores a conversation turn and stable subject identity, provisions the existing conversation backend, runs the turn through software-agent-sdk, records normal run status and telemetry, and releases a completed Docker runtime while retaining conversation history.

Local admission should continue preventing overlapping executions of one scanner, while allowing that scanner's independent agent-turn runs to fan out up to the existing global conversation concurrency limit.

Subject identity must include its source so equal opaque keys from GitHub, Slack, or another integration cannot collide. Existing event-triggered conversation continuation should use the same source-aware locking and lookup.

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A queued agent-turn run stores its prompt, wake behavior, source, subject key, profile snapshot, and deterministic conversation ID.
- [ ] The dispatcher executes the stored turn through the existing conversation backend and software-agent-sdk instead of executing the scanner bundle again.
- [ ] Successful turns reach a terminal run state and release Docker runtime resources while conversation history remains.
- [ ] Failed turns mark the subject unavailable for routing and follow existing failure reporting.
- [ ] Local dispatch permits independent agent-turn runs to fan out up to AUTOMATION_CONVERSATION_MAX_CONCURRENT_RUNS while preventing overlapping scanner runs.
- [ ] Subject locks and lookups namespace external keys by source.
- [ ] Existing webhook-created runs snapshot profile and execution mode as scheduled runs already do.
- [ ] PostgreSQL and SQLite migrations and focused tests cover the behavior.

### Additional Context

This is the internal execution prerequisite for #463. #463 adds the scoped API and idempotency record through which a running scanner creates these runs.
title: Run scanner-selected agent turns as tracked child runs
